ce_bugs.text: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is passed the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees in the input to receive the wrong email template (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail)
Email sending failures are swallowed with a bare `console.log` that doesn't even log the error object, leaving guests persisted but never notified and showing the user a success toast

Non-atomic operation: DB write, calendar update, and email sending are separate steps — if the calendar update fails after the DB write, retries fail with uniqueness errors and the calendar stays permanently out of sync with the DB
EventManager is built from the requester's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the organizer's credentials, so when an attendee calls the endpoint the calendar guest list is silently never updated
Stale validation error persists across dialog reopenings — onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not isInvalidEmail, showing the red error banner with no invalid input present

Error toast construction masks real errors — the template literal is never falsy (rendering 'undefined: ...' when err.data?.code is missing), making the fallback dead code, and t(err.message) assumes all backend messages are translation keys
New guests are created with empty names (name: ""), leading to broken greetings like 'Hi ,' and blank names in emails, ICS files, and calendar attendee lists
Unhandled findFirstOrThrow when booking.userId is null (booking.userId || 0 passed as fallback), causing a raw Prisma error and unhandled 500 instead of a typed TRPCError

Authorization logic bug: `&&` used instead of `||` in isTeamAdminOrOwner check, requiring caller to be both admin and owner and incorrectly denying team admins who are not owners the ability to manage guests
Duplicate attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so case-differing duplicate emails slip through
No server-side `.max()` limit or uniqueness refinement on the `guests` array in the schema, allowing duplicate emails within one request to create duplicate attendee rows and send duplicate emails

No server-side cap or rate limit on number of guest emails an attendee can add, enabling email-bombing / forced information-disclosure of full booking details (description, location, video-call credentials) to arbitrary addresses
Calendar update uses the caller's (ctx.user) credentials in the EventManager instead of the organizer's, causing inconsistency or wrong-calendar mutation when invoked by a non-organizer attendee
Email send errors in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed — the error object is discarded and the handler still returns success, leaving guests persisted but never notified
Validation error banner in AddGuestsDialog never clears: setIsInvalidEmail(true) is set on failure but never reset to false, so the error banner persists after the user fixes the input
Dead fallback in showToast: `message` is always truthy so the `||` fallback branch is unreachable
Unbounded guest input array in addGuests.schema.ts (no .max()) allows unbounded DB writes, email blasts, and calendar API calls — self-service DoS amplification vector
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both an admin AND an owner of the team, wrongly rejecting team admins who aren't owners and owners who aren't admins with FORBIDDEN
Calendar update uses ctx.user (the caller's) credentials instead of the organizer's credentials when constructing EventManager, potentially failing or writing to the wrong calendar
Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat the dedupe and blacklist checks (guest not lowercased), allowing blacklist bypass and duplicate attendee rows

Original unfiltered guests array (not the filtered uniqueGuests) is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails, causing misclassified email templates and wrong ics status/content for duplicates and blacklisted emails
findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws a raw unhandled Prisma NotFoundError (500) instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null
Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both team admin and team owner, so plain team admins get FORBIDDEN on team bookings they administer

EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's credentials, causing calendar updates to fail to match stored calendar references or create spurious events when a non-organizer adds guests

CalendarEvent (evt) constructed in the handler never sets the team field, so sendAddGuestsEmails branches on calendarEvent.team?.members find nothing and team members other than the organizer receive no notification emails

Case-sensitive email comparison in dedupe and blacklist checks allows blacklisted emails with different casing to bypass the blacklist, duplicate attendees to be inserted, and existing attendees to receive 'new guest' emails

Guests input schema is unbounded and permits empty arrays — empty arrays are only rejected after three DB queries with a misleading error code, and no .max() bound allows thousands of guests per request
Attendee-role authorization lets any booking guest (external user with matching email) mutate the organizer's booking and calendar, broadening the trust boundary beyond what the organizer granted
Team permission check uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts, requiring user to be both admin AND owner instead of admin OR owner, denying legitimate team admins
EventManager is constructed with the calling user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, causing calendar updates to use wrong or missing credentials when attendees add guests

DB write of attendees is not transactional with the calendar update, so a calendar API failure leaves guests persisted in DB without being added to external calendars, showing the user an error despite the change being applied
Email send failure is swallowed and the captured err object is never logged, making production debugging impossible and leaving guests silently unnotified
Unhandled findFirstOrThrow on organizer lookup throws raw Prisma NotFoundError when booking.userId is null, resulting in an unhelpful INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a proper TRPCError
Calendar update and CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST email run without checking booking state, so cancelled or past bookings trigger confirmed invites for dead events
sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, causing filtered-out existing attendees to receive duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmations

Case-sensitive email comparison in attendee dedupe check (guest === attendee.email) fails to match differently-cased emails, creating duplicate attendee rows and double invites; client-side Set dedupe is also case-sensitive
Validation error in AddGuestsDialog is set but never cleared on retry or dialog reopen, leaving stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner and dirty state after successful mutation
Guests created with empty name: "" which produces malformed recipient headers in AttendeeScheduledEmail (" <email>") and nameless ICS attendees, needing a fallback like email local part

Authorization logic bug in addGuests.handler.ts:49-51: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both admin and owner, denying team admins who aren't owners with you_do_not_have_permission

Validation schema duplicated between client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) and server (addGuests.schema.ts), and they've diverged: client enforces within-array uniqueness but server doesn't, allowing duplicate attendees to be created via API

Blacklist email comparison in addGuests.handler.ts is case-sensitive against a lowercased list, so 'User@Example.com' bypasses a blacklisted 'user@example.com'; email comparisons should normalize case first

Stale error state in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is never cleared when the user edits input, so the error banner stays visible even after input becomes valid; should be derived from or cleared by changes to multiEmailValue and reset on dialog reopen

Handler passes raw guests to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of filtered uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees whose emails were redundantly typed to receive the full 'booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification
Team permission check uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring the user to be both admin and owner and incorrectly rejecting team admins who are not owners

Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat the blacklist check (blacklisted emails are lowercased but guest emails are not) and duplicate attendee check (=== instead of case-insensitive comparison), allowing bypass via email casing
No cap on the number of guests added, no check against seatsPerTimeSlot or booking size, enabling email-bombing/abuse via mass attendee insertion and N×M email fan-out on repeated calls
EventManager is constructed from the requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so updateCalendarAttendees may silently no-op or error when called by a non-organizer

Calendar update runs after the DB write and outside any try/catch, so a calendar failure returns an error despite guests being persisted with no rollback; email sending failures are silently swallowed with console.log
No booking status or end-time check, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings, which sends CONFIRMED ICS attachments for cancelled events and re-triggers calendar writes
Attendee permission creates an escalation chain where guests become attendees who can recursively add more guests without organizer involvement
New-guest emails have a malformed To: header with an empty display name (guests created with name: ""), which some SMTP relays reject

sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw guests input instead of uniqueGuests, so filtered-out duplicate/blacklisted emails cause existing attendees to be misclassified as new and resent the full AttendeeScheduledEmail
prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 throws an unhandled 500 error for bookings with null userId instead of a typed TRPCError

AddGuestsDialog state only resets on Cancel and mutation success, so closing via X/Esc/backdrop leaves stale multiEmailValue; the React key={index} on the removable email list is fragile on mid-list removal

mrv_findings.text: `&&` used instead of `||` in team permission check in addGuests.handler.ts:60-63 — variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner requires user to be both admin AND owner, rejecting authorized team admins with FORBIDDEN error

Inconsistent constructor call convention in email-manager.ts:535-543 — OrganizerAddGuestsEmail called with props object while AttendeeScheduledEmail and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail called with two positional arguments; positional calls are type errors and throw at getNodeMailerPayload if forced, so attendees receive no notification

Server schema addGuests.schema.ts:5-7 omits the uniqueness refinement the client applies — duplicate emails in input pass validation and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows, producing duplicate ICS attendees, duplicate emails, and corrupted attendee counts

EventManager in addGuests.handler.ts:148-152 built from the requester's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's — when an attendee adds guests, calendar update runs against wrong credential set and organizer's calendar shows old guest list

findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 in addGuests.handler.ts:69-76 throws unhandled Prisma P2025 error for bookings with null userId, surfacing as opaque internal server error instead of meaningful TRPCError
Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && (AND) instead of || (OR) for isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner, denying team admins who aren't owners access to add guests
sendAddGuestsEmails iterates calendarEvent.team?.members but the CalendarEvent built in the handler never sets the team property, making team-member notification dead code
Handler performs no booking status or date check, allowing guests to be added to cancelled or past bookings which re-sends ICS invites with hardcoded status CONFIRMED
BookingListItem.tsx renders the add_members menu item unconditionally for every booking including cancelled ones
AddGuestsDialog.tsx sets isInvalidEmail true but never clears it on success, retry, or change, leaving the error banner visible after a successful add
Blacklist and duplicate attendee checks are case-sensitive: blacklist is lowercased but guest email is not, and existing-attendee comparison is exact-match, allowing bypass via case changes

No atomicity in the handler: updateCalendarAttendees is not wrapped in try/catch and a failure leaves guests persisted in DB without calendar invites or emails, and retrying yields a misleading BAD_REQUEST error
Error object in catch block for sending AddGuestsEmails is captured but never used, logging only a bare string with no stack, message, or recipient details
Zero tests accompany any of the new files (handler, email templates, MultiEmail component, dialog), missing coverage for permission matrix and dedupe/blacklist filtering
booking.userId null case causes findFirstOrThrow to throw an unhandled Prisma NotFoundError, resulting in an unformatted 500 error to the client
Authorization predicate in addGuests.handler.ts:44-46 uses AND instead of OR, requiring the user to be both team admin AND owner, so team admins (non-owners) are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN

EventManager in addGuests.handler.ts:157-161 is built from the requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so when an attendee adds guests the organizer's calendar event is never updated

Team-member notification path in email-manager.ts:529-535 is unreachable dead code because the CalendarEvent constructed in addGuests.handler.ts never sets a team field, making calendarEvent.team always undefined

Generic MultiEmail component added to the shared @calcom/ui package (with lazy-loading wrapper and generic API) has only one consumer (AddGuestsDialog.tsx), expanding infrastructure beyond the feature's scope
BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS env-config feature ships in the guest management PR with no accompanying requirement, documentation, or schema/env typing, making it untraceable to the stated intent

Blacklist check lowercases the blacklist but compares against cased guest values, and the duplicate check is fully case-sensitive, so the no-duplicates/no-blacklisted-emails invariant is not enforced under case variation
Guest management is add-only with no remove/edit path, reducing 'management' to append-only behavior
Handler reads booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot into evt but never checks it, allowing guests to be added past the seat capacity that the product enforces at booking time
Raw unfiltered guests list is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation they had nothing to do with

Authorization check in addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 uses && instead of ||, requiring a user to be both team admin AND owner, so regular team admins are denied FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's booking
booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0 passes sentinel teamId 0 into team queries for personal bookings, a lookup path that can never succeed

Uniqueness of guests is only enforced client-side in AddGuestsDialog.tsx; the server Zod schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema) has no dedupe refinement, so direct tRPC mutation calls with duplicate emails create duplicate attendee rows
No unique DB constraint on (bookingId, email) backs the attendee uniqueness invariant, creating a racy check-then-insert pattern

EventManager in addGuests.handler.ts:160-165 is built from the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials (booking.user.credentials is included but never used), so calendar updates fail or do nothing when a non-organizer invokes the mutation

Multi-system write in addGuests.handler.ts:138-172 is non-atomic: attendee rows are committed before calendar update, so if updateCalendarAttendees throws the guests are already persisted with no rollback, no calendar invite, and no email
Email sending failure is swallowed by a catch that doesn't even log the error object, and the mutation returns success 'Guests added' while no notification was sent
Duplicate-attendee check at addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 uses case-sensitive exact match (guest === attendee.email), allowing re-adding a guest as a case variant like Bob@gmail.com vs bob@gmail.com
Concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the read-then-createMany window due to lack of unique index, producing duplicate attendees
Blacklist comparison lowercases the env list entries but not the guest input, so mixed-case emails like Blacklisted@Example.com bypass the blacklist entirely

addGuests.handler.ts:167 passes raw guests (not uniqueGuests) to sendAddGuestsEmails, causing already-existing attendees filtered out of the DB write to receive a fresh 'you're booked' AttendeeScheduledEmail

findFirstOrThrow on nullable booking.userId with || 0 fallback throws an unhandled raw Prisma NotFoundError for unassigned/team-held bookings, producing a 500 with no TRPCError conversion or diagnostics

guests array in ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no .max() bound, allowing a single mutation with thousands of guests to materialize thousands of attendee rows, translation loads, and email dispatches on the authed hot path
isInvalidEmail state in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is never cleared on successful retry, so the error banner persists after a successful resubmission, and reopening the dialog shows stale error state
Authorization check isTeamAdminOrOwner uses AND instead of OR, requiring the user to be both team admin and team owner rather than either, blocking admins who are not owners from adding guests
Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat both the blacklist check and the duplicate guard — blacklisted emails can be bypassed and duplicate attendee records created by capitalizing letters

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw unfiltered input instead of the actually-added uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees whose emails were re-submitted to receive a full booking re-confirmation email with a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST

Silent partial success: when some guests are filtered out (duplicates/blacklisted), the handler adds only the remainder but returns a flat success message, leaving dropped emails invisible to the user
evt never sets the team field, so the team-member notification branch in email-manager.ts (OrganizerAddGuestsEmail loop over team members) is dead code and team members are never notified

No booking-status check in the findFirst query, allowing guests to be added to cancelled or past bookings, which creates attendee rows and sends CONFIRMED ICS re-confirmation emails for cancelled events
Any attendee of any booking can call the mutation directly with no scoping, letting a non-organizer booker add arbitrary guests and trigger calendar updates and emails on the organizer's calendars
New guests are persisted with empty names, degrading downstream email greetings, calendar invite metadata, and creating permanent attendee records with blank names

Guests array in addGuests.schema.ts has no .max() limit and the handler has no rate limiting, allowing any authenticated attendee to mass-send emails with full meeting details (including video call URL and password) to arbitrary third-party addresses

Email comparisons in addGuests.handler.ts are case-sensitive: blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are compared verbatim, allowing blacklist bypass via mixed-case input like Blocked@Example.com
Case-sensitive email comparison in attendee dedup check (guest === attendee.email) allows case-variant duplicates of existing attendees to be added, e.g., Alice@x.com when alice@x.com already exists

Intra-array duplicate emails pass server validation since uniqueness is enforced only client-side via .refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, causing createMany to insert identical attendee rows and send duplicate emails
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both team admin and owner rather than either, denying team admins who are not owners
Attendee-level privilege allows unilateral disclosure of the organizer's event details to arbitrary emails with no organizer consent or approval step
No check that the booking is upcoming or non-cancelled before allowing guest additions, so the same disclosure works on cancelled or past bookings
Error sending AddGuestsEmails is swallowed with only a console.log in the catch block, ignoring send failures
getUsersCredentials uses the caller's rather than the organizer's credentials for eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, likely causing failure or no-op for non-organizer callers

isTeamAdminOrOwner permission check uses && , requiring the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously, which is suspicious and likely should be || , potentially blocking legitimate admins or owners from adding guests

Potential data-testid collision: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:88 uses data-testid="add_members" on the Add button while BookingListItem.tsx:193 uses id: "add_members" for its dropdown entry; if DropdownMenuItem forwards item.id to data-testid, two elements would share the same ambiguous testid, which also collides with the unrelated team 'add members' feature

Non-atomic multi-step write in addGuests.handler.ts (~105-126): the createMany commits before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails run, so a failure in those steps leaves attendee rows permanently in the DB with no calendar update or emails, and retry becomes impossible because uniqueGuests filters out already-added guests and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, leaving a half-migrated state with no repair path
getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) is called even when ctx.user is only an attendee, so an attendee-triggered add uses the attendee's credentials which frequently have no calendar integration

TOCTOU race on the duplicate filter in addGuests.handler.ts (~85-90): dedup is done in application code against a booking snapshot with no unique constraint or upsert, so concurrent addGuests calls (e.g. double-clicking Add) both pass the filter and create duplicate (bookingId, email) rows that propagate to calendar and email lists with no cleanup path

Silent partial application of guests: the filter silently removes already-existing emails (e.g. existing@y.com) and the mutation returns 'Guests added', giving the user no way to know only a subset was applied; the result should report added vs skipped

Notification failure swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts (~170-174): sendAddGuestsEmails errors are reduced to a console.log that drops the error object, the handler still returns success, and there is no retry, dead-letter record, or 'added but never notified' state marking

Missing seat capacity enforcement in addGuests.handler.ts (~65-68): the handler reads booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot but never enforces it before createMany, creating plain Attendee rows on the parent booking that overbook past the seat limit and are disconnected from seat tracking (seatReferenceUid), violating a data invariant other code paths rely on
